title: Notarizing macOS software before distribution
key_points: Notarization of macOS software is not App Review, but an automated system that scans the software for malicious content and checks for code-signing issues.
When a user installs or runs Developer ID-signed software, Gatekeeper can check if Apple has notarized it, and display descriptive information in the initial launch dialog.
You can notarize macOS apps, non-app bundles like kernel extensions, disk images (UDIF format), and flat installer packages.
Starting November 1, 2023, Apple notary service no longer accepts uploads from `altool` or Xcode 13 or earlier.
limitations: Some preexisting software might not run properly after being successfully notarized.
Notarization also protects users only if Developer ID signing key is exposed.
asserts: Submitting macOS software to Apple for notarization gives users more confidence in the software's safety before distribution.
